title: Scope of this handbook
text: This handbook explains how time off works for US employees under policy TIMEOFF-US-2026.2. The policy rules decide whether a request is allowed; this handbook explains how to apply them and what options exist when a rule is not met.

title: PTO accrual
text: PTO accrues at 6.67 hours per month for employees with under five years of service and 10 hours per month after five years. Accrual is credited on the last day of each month. Balances cannot go negative and PTO cannot be advanced against future accrual.

title: PTO carryover
text: Up to 40 hours of unused PTO carries over into the next calendar year. Hours above the carryover limit are forfeited on 31 December unless HR approves an extension for a documented business reason.

title: Unpaid leave for a balance shortfall
text: When a request exceeds the employee's PTO balance, the manager may approve the paid portion up to the balance and agree the remaining days as unpaid leave. Unpaid leave of more than five working days also needs HR Partner agreement. The request cannot be approved as fully paid.

title: Exceptions to restricted periods
text: Time off during a financial close window needs an approved exception. Exceptions are usually granted for major life events such as weddings, bereavement or medical needs, provided the employee's close tasks are handed to a named backup before the window starts. Routine vacation during close is normally declined or moved.

title: How to approve a close-window exception
text: The manager and the Finance close lead both approve a close-window exception. Record the backup's name and the handoff date in the request comments before approving.

title: Advance notice
text: Give at least 14 days' notice for time off longer than three consecutive days. Managers may accept shorter notice for life events or dates outside the employee's control.

title: Managing team coverage
text: If approving a request would leave fewer than 60 percent of the team available on any working day, the manager may still approve it with a documented backup plan, or ask the employee to move the dates. If nobody on the team would be available, arrange on-call cover from an adjacent team before approving.

title: Extended time off
text: Requests longer than 15 consecutive calendar days are reviewed by an HR Partner. The manager records a recommendation, and the HR Partner checks whether a formal leave of absence is more appropriate than PTO.

title: HR Partner checklist for extended leave
text: For requests over 15 days, check leave-of-absence eligibility, statutory family and medical leave entitlements, benefits continuation and the return-to-work date before advising the manager.

title: Sick leave
text: Sick leave is a separate plan from PTO. Employees receive 40 hours per year. A doctor's note is required only for absences longer than three consecutive working days.

title: Bereavement leave
text: Employees may take up to five paid days of bereavement leave for an immediate family member, separate from PTO. Bereavement leave is not subject to restricted periods.

title: Company holidays
text: Company holidays are published each December for the following year. A holiday inside a PTO request is not deducted from the PTO balance.

title: Balance shortfall (other tenant)
text: Any shortfall in PTO balance is automatically converted to unpaid leave and the request is approved without manager review.

title: Restricted periods (other tenant)
text: This company has no restricted periods. Time off during financial close is approved like any other request.
